newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean police enter secretive German colony.
newsitem.headline: Chilean police enter secretive German colony.

text.p: A large contingent of Chilean police on Tuesday entered the grounds of a secretive German colony in southern Chile in search of its fugitive leader, but later retreated.

A convoy of police vans and trucks passed the colony's first gate but stopped short of an inner gate. The contingent later turned back and Chilean television said the police were merely carrying out a "visual inspection" of the settlement.
Church bells rang out inside the colony and residents lit a huge bonfire, signalling their alarm at the prospect of being stormed by police.
Tension has been building for days around the heavily-guarded Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), whose German founder Paul Schaeffer is wanted on child abuse and other charges.
Schaeffer is believed to be holed up inside the sprawling estate surrounded by barbed wire fences in the foothills of the Andes near the town of Parral, 320 km (200 miles) south of Santiago.
Police have been rumoured to be preparing to storm the colony one week after Schaeffer issued a blistering statement saying he feared for his life if he turned himself in.

Two confidants, both German citizens, and two Chilean members of the settlement surrendered to police last week on charges that include illegal detention of a child, obstruction of justice and destruction of public property. All four were later released on bail but Schaeffer remains at large.
Schaeffer, who is believed to be in his early 80's, set up the colony in the mid-1950's. The mysterious community was protected by the past military regime of Gen. Augusto Pinochet.

A special prosecutor, appointed by President Eduardo Frei's government, issued an arrest warrant for Schaeffer late last year on charges that he molested Chilean boys whose parents had sent them to a boarding school on the colony.
The child abuse charges alienated the colony's one-time allies among conservative Chilean politicians and the Roman Catholic Church, who have urged Schaeffer to give up.
A Chilean cameraman for a German television crew was bashed on the head by one of the colony's security men on Sunday and suffered from concussion.
The attack was strongly condemned by local politicians and media and the Chilean Foreign Press Association.
